description: Single-panel scatter plot (density vs aluminium content) with one fitted calculation curve; no gridlines, inward-pointing ticks on all four frame edges. The x-axis is labelled "wt.-% Al" with integer ticks 5 to 13; the y-axis is labelled "Density (g/cm³)" with ticks 6.4, 6.6, 6.8, 7.0, 7.2, 7.4, 7.6. Two marker series are distinguished only by an in-panel legend at the upper left: open triangles labelled "Al-Fe experimental data compiled by Frommeyer and Drewes (2000)", and open squares labelled "0.2C-8.5Mn alloys" (this text placed in the upper right area). The continuous solid black line runs from about the 7.3 g/cm³ gridline at 5 wt.% Al down to roughly 6.55 g/cm³ at 13 wt.% Al. Triangles and squares both follow that downward trend: values lie above the 7.2 gridline near 6 wt.% Al and fall to about 6.6 g/cm³ near 12 wt.% Al, with most points close to the calculated line. Two points sit clearly above the line: a triangle near the 7.5 gridline at about 11 wt.% Al and a square near the 7.4 gridline at about 10.3 wt.% Al. The figure demonstrates that increasing Al content monotonically lowers density in Fe-Al-based alloys and that measured quaternary 0.2C-8.5Mn alloys track the Thermo-Calc prediction.

subfigures.description: Scatter plot of Density (g/cm³, y-axis 6.4-7.6) versus wt.-% Al (x-axis 5-13). Open triangles = 'Al-Fe experimental data compiled by Frommeyer and Drewes (2000)'; open squares = '0.2C-8.5Mn alloys'. A continuous black line (Thermo-Calc calculation per caption) decreases monotonically across the composition range. Most markers hug the line; one triangle (~11 wt.% Al) and one square (~10.3 wt.% Al) lie well above it.

observations.observation: The x-axis is labelled 'wt.-% Al' and is ticked at integer values from 5 to 13.
The y-axis is labelled 'Density (g/cm³)' and is ticked from 6.4 to 7.6 in steps of 0.2.

Two data series are plotted: open triangles and open squares; the legend text inside the upper-left of the plot reads 'Al-Fe experimental data compiled by Frommeyer and Drewes (2000)' for the triangles and '0.2C-8.5Mn alloys' for the squares.

Both marker series show density decreasing with increasing Al content: points lie above the 7.2 g/cm³ gridline near 6 wt.% Al and drop to about 6.6 g/cm³ near 12 wt.% Al, i.e. all experimental points fall close to the solid line over the plotted range.
A single open triangle at roughly 11 wt.% Al sits near the 7.5 g/cm³ gridline, far above the decreasing trend line, and is the clearest high outlier in the plot.
An open square at roughly 10.3 wt.% Al sits near the 7.4 g/cm³ gridline, also well above the trend line, and is adjacent to the '0.2C-8.5Mn alloys' legend text.
A single continuous solid black line decreases monotonically from the left edge (just above the 7.2 g/cm³ gridline at 5 wt.% Al) to roughly 6.55 g/cm³ at 13 wt.% Al.
No numeric values are printed on individual data points; only axis ticks and the legend text carry quantitative information.
The caption states the quaternary 0.2C-8.5Mn (wt.%) alloys were evaluated by picnometry.
The caption states the continuous line corresponds to the density calculation for the quaternary system using Thermo-Calc.
The caption states the triangle data are binary Fe-Al data from reference 18 (Frommeyer et al.).

The citing text asserts that the experimental data in Fig. 1 seem to indicate a slightly lower density of the quaternary alloys in comparison with the binary Fe-Al alloys, possibly an effect of Mn or of the two data sets coming from different sources.
The citing text states the Thermo-Calc calculation used the database with the latest assessment by Lindahl and Selleby together with volume data from the commercial Thermo-Calc database.
